body:
## Pull request overview

This PR modernizes the console list page by introducing a design mode toggle and improving the metadata inspector panel, following modern SaaS design patterns from companies like Linear, Vercel, and Stripe. The changes separate end-user runtime UI from developer tools, reducing visual clutter and implementing progressive disclosure.

**Changes:**
- Added design mode toggle with dropdown menu to hide developer tools from end users by default
- Modernized metadata inspector with collapsible sections, copy-to-clipboard functionality, and cleaner visual design
- Reduced metadata panel width from w-100 (25rem) to w-80 (20rem) and changed styling to lighter, more subtle backgrounds
- Added comprehensive UI improvement proposal documentation

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 8 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/console/src/components/ObjectView.tsx | Implemented design mode toggle with dropdown menu; replaced always-visible tool buttons with progressive disclosure pattern; metadata panel now only shows in design mode |
| apps/console/src/components/MetadataInspector.tsx | Added collapsible sections with chevron indicators; implemented copy-to-clipboard with visual feedback (Copy→Check icon); reduced visual weight with lighter backgrounds and improved typography |
| apps/console/docs/UI_IMPROVEMENT_PROPOSAL.md | New comprehensive design proposal documenting current issues, design principles, implementation phases, competitive analysis, and success metrics |
| apps/console/README.md | Updated developer tools feature description to mention new collapsible sections and copy functionality |
| PULL_REQUEST_SUMMARY.md | New summary document with visual comparisons and impact metrics |
</details>

The "Metadata Inspector" menu item is missing an icon while the other menu items (Edit View, Add View) have icons with the "mr-2" spacing class. For consistency with the rest of the menu, add an icon (likely Code2 or similar) before the text to match the visual pattern.

The new design mode toggle functionality lacks test coverage. Consider adding tests for:
- Default state (design mode = false)
- Toggling design mode via the dropdown menu
- Metadata panel visibility tied to design mode state
- Menu icon changes between MoreVertical and Wrench based on design mode

The existing ObjectView.test.tsx file shows the codebase has comprehensive test coverage for other features, so this new functionality should also be tested.

The new MetadataInspector features lack test coverage:
- Collapsible sections functionality (expand/collapse behavior)
- Copy to clipboard with visual feedback (Copy icon → Check icon)
- Default expanded state (first section expanded by default)
- Multiple section state management

The console app has comprehensive test coverage (23 test files) for other components, so these new features should also be tested.

The collapsible section buttons should have proper ARIA attributes for accessibility. Add `aria-expanded={isExpanded}` to the toggle button and consider wrapping in a proper semantic element like `<summary>` if appropriate, or at minimum add `role="button"` and `aria-label` with descriptive text for screen readers.

The copy button should have better accessibility. Add `aria-label` that changes based on the copied state (e.g., "Copy JSON" when not copied, "Copied!" when copied) to provide feedback to screen reader users about the action's success.

The state initialization for `expandedSections` and `copiedIndex` inside the MetadataPanel component means that state will be reset every time the panel is closed and reopened. This provides a fresh start each time but may not be the ideal user experience.

Consider whether users would benefit from the panel remembering which sections were expanded when they reopen it. If persistence is desired, the state should be lifted to a parent component or stored in localStorage.

The MetadataToggle component renders a Button, which creates nested interactive elements when used inside a DropdownMenuItem. This causes invalid HTML (button inside button) and accessibility issues.

Instead, the DropdownMenuItem should directly handle the toggle action and display appropriate text/icons without nesting the MetadataToggle component. The menu item should just call toggleDebug directly in its onClick handler, similar to how the other menu items work.
